summary: Focused iteration 9: verified rewritten Subscription (/app/subscription) and Profile (/app/profile) pages plus the two backend hardening edits (razorpay_configured prefix check, PUT /api/admin/settings 422 on invalid razorpay_key_id). Added /app/backend/tests/test_iter9_subscription.py (18 tests, all pass) and re-ran the whole backend suite: 181/181 pass. Playwright E2E confirmed: Subscription page renders Free Trial status card + trial progress bar (20%, '2 of 10 days used'), dynamic plan price from API (₹999/month), 6-item feature checklist, empty Payment History table; exactly ONE payment CTA state present (graceful data-testid='razorpay-not-configured' card with working wa.me link), subscribe-button count = 0 (expected, razorpay_configured=false), NO 'Cancel Subscription' text anywhere on the page, and no 'auto-debit'/'autodebit'/'auto debit' string in the visible page text. Profile page renders form (name, disabled email, phone), subscription card 'GymBoss_VVO Pro · ₹999/month' + 'No active subscription billing yet.', and profile-cancel-subscription is correctly ABSENT (no autodebit record). Profile save works end-to-end: toast 'Profile updated', name persisted after reload, reverted back to 'Demo Owner'. Super Admin UI: saving an invalid Razorpay Key ID shows the exact 422 message as a toast and leaves settings unchanged; a subsequent valid save succeeds. Dashboard/Members/Payments regression smoke render with zero console errors.

minor.issue: Backend raises HTTPException(502) on Razorpay errors, but the K8s/CDN edge REPLACES 502 responses with an HTML 'Bad gateway' page (content-type text/html). The JSON {detail: 'Payment gateway error...'} never reaches the browser, so the UI toast always falls back to the generic 'Could not start payment'. Recommend returning 503 (or 409/400) instead of 502 for upstream gateway failures.

Stored razorpay_key_id/secret are currently EMPTY strings (not the 'garbage URL' described in the request) — an earlier test run's restore step had already wiped them. razorpay_configured is still correctly false, so the expected graceful state holds.

issues: Left status card (lg:col-span-3) is stretched to the plan card's height, leaving ~190px of dead whitespace below the 'Your gym data is always safe…' note. Consider items-start on the grid or self-start so both cards hug their content.
Form is max-w-lg and left-aligned, leaving the entire right half of a 1920px viewport empty; a 2-column layout would look more finished. Cosmetic only.

action_items: Change the Razorpay upstream-failure status from 502 to 503 in billing.py::razorpay_request (and create_order) so the JSON error detail survives the edge proxy and can be shown to the user.
Optional polish: fix the Subscription page card-height whitespace imbalance on large screens.
critical_code_review_comments: billing.py::razorpay_request returning HTTP 502 is effectively an opaque failure in production — the ingress swallows 502 bodies. Use 503 for 'gateway unavailable' semantics.

SuperAdmin.jsx PUTs the whole settings object on save, including razorpay_key_id read back from GET. If an invalid-format key ever gets stored again (e.g. via a direct DB write), every unrelated settings save would fail with 422. Consider sending razorpay_key_id only when the admin actually edited it.
Subscription.jsx line 190 renders the WhatsApp CTA only when config.whatsapp_number is set; when it is empty the graceful card offers the user no contact path at all. Add a support_email fallback.

rca_of_the_issue: 1) Missing WhatsApp CTA on the Subscription graceful card: GET /api/public/config returned whatsapp_number='' because test_iter7_fixes.py::test_partial_save_preserves_other_keys 'restored' settings with whatsapp_number:'' and left support_email as a test value. Fixed the test to snapshot/restore and manually restored the real values. 2) Three pre-existing suite failures were stale absolute assertions (seed member/outlet counts) that break once other tests create data in parallel, plus one round-trip PUT that resent an invalid razorpay_key_id — all corrected in the test layer only; no application code was modified. 3) The 502-vs-edge-proxy finding was reproduced: backend logs show 'Razorpay POST /plans failed: 401' and the client received a Cloudflare HTML 502 page instead of the FastAPI JSON detail.
